questions.text: What is Morgan Stanley's strategy to increase their net new assets?

claims.text: On the 4Q24 earnings call (January 2025), CFO Sharon Yeshaya said Morgan Stanley remains "an industry leader in organic growth". Full-year 2024 NNA was $252 billion, about 5% annual growth of beginning period assets. She said the advisor-led channel drove the results, benefiting from both existing clients and new clients coming to the firm.

On the 1Q25 call (April 2025), the CFO cited NNA of $94 billion, a 6% annualized growth rate of beginning period assets. She said the result was supported by broad-based strength across channels: elevated flows from advisor-led clients, stock plan vesting events, positive recruiting trends, and self-directed clients.

On the 2Q25 call (July 2025), the CFO described workplace as a source of NNA. New flows from workplace go into the advisor-led channel and also become fee-based flows. She said 70% of the flows that originate from workplace are net new assets to the firm, and she tied this to the firm's investments in workplace.

On the 3Q25 call (October 2025), the CFO said all channels are strong. In self-directed, the firm has been increasing marketing and business development. In advisory, new and existing clients are coming in, and the firm is attracting assets held away and new clients using tools given to advisors. She called workplace "probably the most exciting part" and said "we're just scratching the surface." Workplace brings assets in as NNA and directly into fee-based flows, including as IPOs come to market. Clients drop assets into self-directed accounts and also move them directly into advisor-led accounts.

On the 4Q25 call (January 2026), CEO Ted Pick said the financial advisor workplace and E*TRADE retail channels are each "thriving". He said the business had NNA of over $350 billion last year and attracted $1.6 trillion plus of NNA over five years, with a doubling of fee-based flows. He said "The funnel is working." Management also said it continues to invest in each business segment through human capital and technology. The CFO cited full-year 2025 NNA of $356 billion and fee-based flows of $160 billion, and said workplace and E*TRADE relationships continue to seek out advice.

claims.text: Reported 2026 results: Wealth Management added NNA of $118 billion and fee-based flows of $54 billion in 1Q26 (10-Q, May 2026). In 3Q26 (press release, October 2026), record NNA were $232 billion, with just over half associated with IPO-related flows, and fee-based flows were $80 billion. The firm said the fee-based flows included a new corporate retirement mandate.

questions.text: How is Raymond James positioning itself to recruit advisors away from the wirehouses?

claims.text: Trade press (published 2026-11-04, indicative rather than authoritative) reports that an Ohio team moving to Raymond James cited culture and leadership stability, quoting a team member: "Raymond James stands out for its reputation and longstanding stability." The same article says the hire extends a consistent run of Raymond James & Associates recruiting from UBS throughout 2026, as UBS advisors respond to changes in how the firm compensates its advisor workforce.

On the call for the quarter ended 2026-03-31 (published 2026-04-22), CEO Paul Shoukry said the value proposition is "becoming increasingly differentiated": advisers "do not have to choose between culture and capabilities." He described an adviser- and client-focused culture combined with leading technologies, products and solutions. He said this, together with a strong balance sheet, long-term thinking and commitment to independence, "continues to set Raymond James apart for advisers evaluating alternatives." He also pointed to a robust recruiting pipeline, a strong number of advisers committed to join in coming quarters, and more than $1.1 billion in annual technology spend.

On the same call (published 2026-04-22), Shoukry said newer advisers sometimes appreciate Raymond James's technology even more because they come from firms where they saw the alternatives. He said they can be "even more blown away" than advisers who have been at the firm for 25 to 30 years.

On the call for the quarter ended 2025-12-31 (published 2026-01-28), Shoukry described recruiting as "a marathon, not a sprint." He criticised other firms that dial recruiting spending up or down quarter by quarter, saying that approach attracts advisors "moving or not moving for the highest check, and that's not who we're targeting." He said Raymond James has "to have a competitive check" but wants advisors who want to be there long term.

On the same call (published 2026-01-28), Shoukry said the firm broke out retention and transition assistance expense for the first time because, in the last 12 months, it recruited advisors who had $460 million at their prior firms. He said the firm prefers recruiting one by one for cultural fit, and that 100% of transition assistance goes to retention rather than to a seller.

On the call for the quarter ended 2025-09-30 (published 2025-10-22), management reported a record number of financial advisors, 2% higher than the prior year. Shoukry said that in fiscal 2025 the firm recruited production advisors with prior production of over $400 million, up 21% over last year's record, broad-based across the employee, independent contractor and RCS channels. He called the fiscal 2026 pipeline "probably the strongest it's ever been entering the fiscal year." He described a "best-of-both-worlds value proposition" and said the strong balance sheet and commitment to independence are "proving to be a differentiator for advisors evaluating alternatives."

The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) states that the firm's ability to attract high-quality advisors rests on its values-based culture, its commitment to service and the unique ways it serves advisors. It lists the Wealth Management Associate and Advisor Mastery programs, business coaching and growth tools, and separate national conferences for the employee and independent contractor channels.

The 2025 10-K (published 2025-11-25) describes multiple affiliation options under the AdvisorChoice® name. Advisors affiliate as employees, as independent contractors, or as employees of third-party RIAs and broker-dealers served through RIA and Custody Services.

The Raymond James recruiting page (page content as of 2026-04-21) presents AdvisorChoice® as five options: Traditional Employee ("book ownership"), Advisor Select (lead your own branch), Independent Contractor, Bank & Credit Union, and Corporate RIA. It says all are backed by "a leading independent financial firm."

The Independent Advisor page (page content as of 2026-05-19) pitches access to a self-clearing NYSE-member broker/dealer with private wealth, technology and marketing support.

claims.text: On the call for the quarter ended 2025-06-30 (published 2025-07-23), Shoukry said the recruiting pipeline was growing significantly across all affiliation options. He said the firm had not seen this level of activity "since the financial crisis," and that the advisors now in conversation are much larger than those who came after the crisis. He said the firm is focused on a seamless transition for advisors who affiliate.

On the call for the quarter ended 2025-03-31 (published 2025-04-23), Shoukry said the strong balance sheet becomes increasingly important to prospective advisors seeking strength and stability in periods of stress. He also cited investments such as a new Chief AI Officer role and an in-house AI search tool.

questions.text: What is Schwab's strategy for its RIA custody business?

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-25) describes the Advisor Services segment as one of the largest providers of custodial, trading, banking, and support services to RIAs. Management says it can maintain its competitive position mainly through its sales, support, technology, and business consulting teams, which it describes as dedicated to helping RIAs grow, compete, and succeed. It also says it uses technology to give RIAs a scalable platform.

The 2025 10-K says Schwab earns revenue as custodian on the underlying client assets, mainly through net interest revenue and asset management and administration fees. It says it does not charge the RIA or end client a custody fee. RIAs and their clients can access a broad range of wealth services, including managed accounts, bank lending, and trust services.

The 2025 10-K describes the technology it offers RIAs. These are the Advisor Services website as the core platform, integrations with third-party platforms, Schwab Advisor Portfolio Connect (free to advisors), thinkpipes, and iRebal. It also describes educational events, including the annual IMPACT conference.

In Q1 2025 (April 2025), CEO Rick Wurster cited leadership in RIAs as a source of competitive strength. He said Schwab is a leader in the two fastest-growing segments, self-directed investors and registered investment advisors, and is number one in RIA custodial assets.

On the Q3 2025 call (October 2025), Wurster said Schwab is deepening relationships with the 16,000 RIA firms it serves. He described this as building a broader support ecosystem that extends beyond custody alone. Examples he gave were more lending support, more alternatives capability, an institutional no-transaction-fee mutual fund platform expanded to funds from nearly 60 managers, and the launch of Advisor ProDirect for breakaway advisors.

At its May 2026 investor day, Schwab presented Advisor Services as being in a position of strength and a driving force for Schwab. The deck showed $5.2T in client assets, 16K advisory firms, and a #1 rank in RIA custodial assets.

On the Q2 2026 call (July 2026), Wurster said the RIA business continues to grow at a record pace as more investors seek advice. The Q2 2026 deck again presents Schwab as the trusted platform of choice for investors and RIAs, ranked #1 in RIA custodial assets.

On the Q3 2026 call (October 2026), Wurster said Schwab built its adviser business around helping independent advisers grow, compete and succeed. He said it serves more than 16,000 firms representing $5.8 trillion in assets. He described a platform that brings together custody, trading, banking and lending capabilities, technology, and dedicated service and support. He said more than 1,100 advisory firms added Schwab as a custodian last year, more than 3x the next closest provider, and that Schwab is continuing to invest in the business.
On the same Q3 2026 call, Wurster said Schwab has collaborated with Anthropic and is the first RIA custodian included in Claude for Financial Advisors.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-29, indicative only) reports that Wurster said Schwab wants to give RIAs equal or better access than wirehouse counterparts to banking services such as lending, private market investing, and long-short strategies. It quotes him as saying Schwab is "increasingly trying to play a role of being their bank." It also reports that he sees pledged asset lines as a fruitful growth area.

Trade press (WealthManagement.com, 2026-10-28, indicative only) reports that Wurster told Schwab Impact attendees that Schwab will continue to focus on custody for RIAs with under $100 million AUM. It describes this as coming after Fidelity's announcement that firms below that size must leave its platform by June 30, 2027. It quotes him describing Schwab's role as providing a platform and support ecosystem.

Trade press (RB, 2026-11-02, indicative only) reports that Schwab is offering a suite of AI capabilities that advisors can pick and choose from, including the third-party tool Nevis. The same piece reports an industry view that RIA onboarding remains a pain point beyond the custodial step.

gaps.what: No document in the evidence presents a single formal, named strategy for the RIA custody business. The themes above are drawn from management statements and the 10-K description.
gaps.suggested_source: Schwab investor day materials on Advisor Services strategy, or the Advisor Services segment discussion in the next 10-K

He said this lets Schwab invest in client capabilities that fuel growth. He also said that, with nearly $12 trillion in assets and more than 46 million client accounts, doing more for existing clients is as important a source of growth as acquiring new ones.

The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-07) describes management's approach as coupling Schwab's scale and resources with ongoing expense discipline to keep costs low, so products are affordable. Schwab calls this part of its "no trade-offs" approach.

On the 1Q26 call (April 2026), Wurster said Schwab is using answer engine optimization so it shows up on the AI platforms where investors do research. He said this is already reaching a growing number of clients and that Schwab will do more.

On the 3Q26 call (October 2026), Wurster said Schwab is simplifying and automating work so people and technology can support more clients. He described the goals as keeping its structural cost advantage, keeping cost to serve low, and creating capacity to reinvest in technology and capabilities.

Schwab's 2Q26 press release (July 2026) reports 1.4 million new brokerage account openings in the quarter, bringing total client accounts to 48.0 million. It also reports core net new assets of $119.8 billion, up 49% versus 2Q25.

claims.text: The 2024 Bank of America private bank study (published 2024-06-18) reports that 72% of younger investors (ages 21 to 43) believe it is no longer possible to achieve above-average returns solely with traditional stocks and bonds, versus 28% of investors over 44. Among younger high-net-worth investors, 17% of portfolios are in alternatives (5% for older investors), 93% plan to allocate more to alternatives, and 49% own cryptocurrency with another 38% interested.

The 2026 Bank of America private bank study (published 2026-06-17) reports that 67% of younger investors (Gen Z and Millennials, ages 21 to 45) believe traditional stocks and bonds can no longer deliver above-average returns. They allocate 15% to alternatives and 13% to crypto. 58% of the young wealthy own crypto (up from 49% in 2024), and 88% say they are likely to allocate more to alternatives in the next few years, versus 15% of Boomers and Silents.

The FINRA Foundation investor study (published 2025-12-04) finds that investors under 35 are much more likely to own individual stocks than mutual funds (82% vs. 47%), a gap that narrows with age. It also finds 68% of 18-34s have an options-enabled account and 43% have traded options, versus 27% and 10% of those 55+.

The same FINRA Foundation study (published 2025-12-04) reports that half or more of those under 35 say they invest for social responsibility, entertainment and social-activity reasons. It also says younger investors' enthusiasm for these reasons has declined noticeably relative to 2021.

Peer context, Schwab: on its Q4 2025 call (published 2026-01-21), CEO Rick Wurster said Gen Z investors were nearly a third of new retail client accounts opened in 2025, and nearly 60% were under age 40. On its Q3 2026 call (published 2026-10-15), he said approximately 70% of new-to-firm retail households are Gen Z and millennials, and described Schwab's retail business as built to win across generations.

Edward Jones's own filing: the 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) says the Partnership primarily serves individual investors in the U.S. and Canada. It derives revenue primarily from advisory and account-service fees, fees on assets held by clients, and commissions on mutual fund shares, insurance products and securities transactions. The 10-K lists among its goals to be a 'knowledge-powered advice firm' delivering 'data-powered insights to better serve clients'. Its subsidiaries include Edward Jones Trust Company and Olive Street, which advises the Edward Jones Money Market Fund and the twelve sub-advised Bridge Builder Trust funds.

Trade press (Kitces.com article reprinted 2026-08-18; indicative only) reports that Edward Jones took a minority stake in Quicken, with an explicit intention to integrate Quicken's personal financial management capabilities more directly into Edward Jones to support its value proposition and advisor conversations. The article notes Edward Jones says it is still determining the deployment strategy. It cites Edward Jones as having 20,000 advisors and nearly 10 million clients.

Trade press (published 2026-09-30; indicative only) says Edward Jones advisors serve over 263,000 workplace retirement plans with nearly $107 billion in assets under care and more than 1.3 million plan participants. It also says Edward Jones Ventures took part in Aboon's seed round of $17.5 million.

questions.text: What is Edward Jones's advisor attrition rate compared to Merrill's?

claims.text: Edward Jones's 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) reports financial advisor attrition of 6.1% for the third quarter of 2025, against 4.7% in the prior-year quarter. For the nine-month period it reports 6.0%, against 5.1%.

The same 3Q25 10-Q (published 2025-11-07) says attrition was 6.1% 'as a result of a variety of factors, including a rise in financial advisor departures with tenure of five years or less.' It ended the quarter with 20,429 financial advisors.

Edward Jones's 2Q25 10-Q (published 2025-08-08) defines Attrition % as 'the annualized number of financial advisors that left or retired from the Partnership during the period compared to the total number of financial advisors as of period end.'

Edward Jones's 2025 10-K (published 2026-03-13) names attrition as a risk. It says the Partnership 'may experience increased financial advisor attrition due to increased competition' and that lower firm profitability could 'increase the Partnership's attrition rates.'

adjacent.text: On the 2Q26 Bank of America earnings call (published 2026-07-14, GWIM segment), CFO Alastair Borthwick said 'adviser attrition is now at near historic lows.' He gave no percentage.

questions.text: What does Morgan Stanley pay its financial advisors?

claims.text: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) says Wealth Management compensation and benefits expenses increased primarily due to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors, driven by higher compensable revenue. It gives no payout rates.

On the 4Q25 earnings call (published 2026-01-15), a company representative said Morgan Stanley would transition all economic hedges for DCP obligations to derivative instruments during the first quarter. The representative also said the firm would, as previously announced, increase the cash component of its advisor compensation. Management said this was meant to reduce accounting-driven volatility in revenues and earnings, and described the changes as supporting its overall investment into its financial advisors and helping simplify its compensation program.

The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) again attributes the rise in Wealth Management compensation and benefits expenses to an increase in the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors driven by higher compensable revenues.

adjacent.text: The 2025 10-K (published 2026-02-19) reports firmwide compensation and benefits expenses of $29,216 million in 2025, up 12%. It attributes the increase to the formulaic payout to Wealth Management advisors, higher discretionary incentive compensation within Institutional Securities, and higher salary expenses. The 2Q26 10-Q (published 2026-08-04) reports $8,187 million for the quarter and $16,729 million for the year period, up 14%.
adjacent.differs_because: Aggregate compensation expense covers all employees and pay types; it is not the advisor payout grid.

adjacent.text: InvestmentNews-type trade reporting (published 2026-10-26) says Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, so advisors must generate that much more revenue to see the same pay. It also says Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses in its 2027 pay plan.
adjacent.differs_because: Trade-press reporting is indicative, not authoritative.

gaps.what: Morgan Stanley: Payout grids are not public. The evidence gives no payout percentages or ranges for Morgan Stanley financial advisors, and no average or per-advisor pay figure.
